subject: MedFusion: request for service resilience addendum + order form language
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfusion.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@medfusion.com
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service resilience addendum & order form language—MedFusion

Jonas,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. Procurement asked me to follow up with a formal request: we need a bespoke SLA addendum that includes (A) a tail-latency SLO for batch inference jobs (99.9th percentile under a specified window), (B) a regional failover commitment for primary->secondary region within X minutes, and (C) a limited credit schedule tied to measurable telemetry.

Specifically, procurement wants proposed order-form language we can drop into our MSA/SOW so legal can run it through DocuSign quickly. I attached our current executed MSA and a draft order form with placeholders. Two quick questions up front: can Redwood commit to a 15-minute RTO for cold-region failover for this workload class, and what telemetry will you provide as evidence (logs, request traces, aggregated p50/p95/p99 token latency)?

We are targeting a mid-May go/no-go for pilot billing to align with a Q3 rollout. If you can send a one-page addendum draft plus the order-form snippets, procurement will expedite.

Best,
Elena
Director, Infrastructure & Procurement
MedFusion Health

Attachments: MedFusion_MSA_Executed.pdf (pdf), MF-orderform-draft-20280408.xlsx (xlsx)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfusion.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service resilience addendum & order form language—MedFusion

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Attaching a proposed SLA addendum and two suggested order-form clauses that map to (A)-(C). High level responses to your quick questions:

- 15-minute cold-region RTO: we can commit to an RTO target of 15 minutes for regional failover for high-availability customers that have enabled cross-region replication and reserved failover capacity in Dedicated. That will be surfaced as an availability exhibit with blackout exceptions for scheduled maintenance and region-level provider outages.

- Telemetry evidence: we will provide an evidence bundle that includes time-series request traces (per-route p50/p95/p99), aggregated token-rate charts, and a signed uptime report for the affected month. For security, sensitive traces are redacted and shared via a secure S3 link or the Redwood Console export.

Notes about credits: our standard order-form ties credits to month-over-month availability deltas and caps cumulative credits at 30% of monthly invoice for the impacted service. We included an alternate schedule in the draft that limits credits for degraded tail-latency only to a narrower band to align incentives.

Next steps I propose: 1) you and procurement review the attached draft addendum and the two order-form snippets, 2) if OK, we route to Karthik (legal) for redlines and then to Marcus (ops) to confirm telemetry delivery windows, 3) finalize DocuSign route.

I attached: redwood-proposed-sla-addendum.docx (word), and an order-form snippet in the body here.

--Jonas
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-sla-addendum.docx (docx)

--- order-form snippet (for insertion into SOW/order form) ---
Service: Redwood Inference — Inference API (Dedicated)
Commitment: 99.95% regional availability per billing month for the Inference API control plane and serving endpoints, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
Tail-latency SLO: 99.9th percentile request completion time below 2.5s for batch inference workloads with per-request concurrency <= 16 and token lengths <= 2048.
Remedy: Availability credits as defined in SLA Addendum, not exceeding 30% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service.
--- end snippet ---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfusion.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service resilience addendum & order form language—MedFusion

Elena, Jonas — looping in a couple of redlines/clarity items from Legal before we finalize. I've marked everything inline in the attached Word draft, but summarizing the key negotiation points here so procurement can react quickly:

1) Definition clarity: we need unambiguous definitions for "batch inference" (max concurrent requests, payload size) so enforcement is deterministic. Suggest we adopt the snippet Jonas proposed (concurrency <=16, token length <=2048) and add a measurement window (five-minute rolling).

2) Failover RTO: Karthik (Legal) recommends softening absolute language around 15-minute RTO — propose "target RTO of 15 minutes for initiated failover, with recovery subject to cloud-provider region constraints and an exclusion for region-wide provider degradations." This keeps expectations realistic while preserving customer value.

3) Evidence delivery timing: MedFusion asked for telemetry; we'll commit to delivering the evidence bundle within 5 business days of a claimed incident, and an expedited 48-hour bundle for Priority incidents (at Redwood's discretion for triage). Please confirm procurement is ok with these windows.

4) Credit schedule: Legal pushed for a hard cap on total annual credits (we propose 120% of one month invoice across the year) plus the per-incident cap Jonas noted. Please review; we can negotiate upward for large enterprise commitments.

Marcus — can you confirm tooling: does operations have a documented export path for per-route p99 traces that we can use as the evidence artifact? If not, we'll need to map an export-runbook before signoff.

K

Attachments: redlined-redwood-sla-addendum.docx (docx)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfusion.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@medfusion.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service resilience addendum & order form language—MedFusion

Jonas / Karthik / Marcus — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear draft. Procurement reviewed the order-form snippet and our legal is OK with the softening of the RTO language as long as there is an explicit maximum time-to-failover (we propose "target 15 minutes; maximum 45 minutes per event unless force majeure" to be acceptable to execs).

Procurement also asked for the 5-business-day evidence window to be automated where possible — is there a standard API or console export we can call for historical p99 traces, or will this be a manual bundle request? If there's an API, please send the endpoint and sample payload.

Assuming we can get the evidence export path and the revised credit cap language updated (we'll accept Redwood's annual cap but please keep per-incident cap at 30% monthly invoice), we can route the final redlined addendum through our DocuSign flow by Friday and target a signature next week. Can you produce the final redline-ready doc with the 45-minute maximum failover cap included?

If you prefer, I can open the DocuSign envelope and invite Redwood as a signer once we have the final file.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Elena
Director, Infrastructure & Procurement
MedFusion Health
